questions: Did the oval and s-bend hold 20/20 finishes under the final controller? Report finish counts, progress and steering_oscillation per track.
Did slalom line-loss fall below 1.1 per run, and do losses cluster at direction changes? Report line_loss_events and off-track counts per track.
Is there any sign of jitter (steering_oscillation above about 0.35 with low max_error) on the sharp tracks? If so, report whether the cause is the controller gains or the 0.5 kg mass.
feedback_request.suggested_changes_to_test: No geometry change is proposed for the final race. If the controller change causes the oval to fall below 16/20 or oscillation to exceed about 0.35 with low max_error, the Integrator should return the controller to the iteration 10 gains rather than alter geometry. Do not change wheel_track, span, footprint, sensor y or mass.

intent: Hold the iteration 10 geometry exactly (five sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 0.015 m steps, y = 0.07 m, sensor_size 0.012 m, wheel_track 0.09 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.5 kg). The Integrator should change only the controller. This gives a stable, robust platform for the unseen final track, and keeps any score change attributable to the controller.
learning: Across iterations 0 to 10, the geometry levers that moved the score were forward sensor position (y 0.06 to 0.07 m, helping the oval), mass 0.7 to 0.5 kg (helping s-bend finishes), and wheel_track narrowing to 0.09 m (small gains). Span, footprint and wheel_radius changes did not help. The controller (kp, kd) produced the largest gains on the sharp tracks. Slalom line-loss has not moved with any geometry change and is probably a controller or line-loss-mode problem.
rationale:
This is the final iteration, and the race is scored on an unseen track of a different shape, so the design should be a robust platform rather than one tuned to the development tracks. Iteration 10 (score 700.7) is the best observed result on this geometry, with the oval at 20/20 and s-bend at 20/20 with line-loss 0.55. Slalom is still 0/20 with line-loss 1.2, which points to the controller's response at direction changes, not the body.

Geometry evidence since iteration 2 is consistent. Span widening (iteration 2) and footprint 0.016 m (iteration 3) both hurt. Forward position 0.07 m (iteration 4) helped the oval. Narrowing wheel_track to 0.09 m (iterations 5 to 6) gave small gains and is at its floor. Mass 0.5 kg (iteration 7) raised s-bend finishes, and the body has since held oscillation at about 0.21 to 0.27 with the stronger controller. Body width does not change the off-track limit, which stays at the 0.06 m floor. Speed is not limiting, since the oval finishes in about 1.96 s.

Decision: hold every geometry value at the iteration 10 best. Changing geometry now would confound the Integrator's last controller step, and the unseen track is best served by a body that is already known to finish the oval and s-bend reliably. Expected result: the same platform scores near 700 on the development tracks, with any further gain coming from the Integrator's controller (kd, line_loss mode) on sharp bends.
